# Where does retrieval coverage come from? User representations, positive examples, and negative difficulty

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/retrieval-matching.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 36 topic entries / 4 representative comparisons

Candidate generation determines what downstream ranking can see. YouTube DNN uses one user vector for nearest-neighbor retrieval; Airbnb EBR ties supervision to the search–browse–booking journey; MIMA allocates multiple positives from a request to complementary interests; MDCNS changes negative difficulty and provides multi-view supervision. These alter representations, labels, interest specialization, and gradients, respectively. More retrieved candidates are not a common explanation.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Locate the bottleneck: coverage, supervision, or interest collapse

YouTube DNN compresses history into one user vector. Airbnb EBR keeps a similar retrieval interface but reorganizes journey supervision. A similar dual-encoder shape does not make their training problems equivalent. MIMA's defining change is one-to-one assignment of same-request positives, not merely emitting more vectors; otherwise interests may converge on one positive. Fix the final return budget to separate better representations from retrieving more items.

Sources: [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md) · [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md)

### Hard negatives and multiple positives have different roles

MDCNS finds unobserved candidates models find difficult and disagree on, giving Self full-pool teacher supervision. MIMA learns interest specialization from real positive sets. Labeling all unclicked items as negatives or treating adjacent behaviors as complementary same-request positives changes the meaning of supervision. Airbnb EBR's journey reminds us to record behavioral stages and exposure before interpreting a lower loss.

Sources: [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If recall rises after MIMA returns multiple interests, how can we distinguish complementarity from a larger candidate budget? {#cross-more-interests-not-more-budget}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Fix total K after merging and deduplicating channels, then compare with single-vector retrieval. Check whether positive assignments and hits complement each other. The mechanism is MIMA's one-to-one supervision and activation calibration; YouTube DNN gives a single-vector starting point. Giving each interest an extra K makes a coverage gain impossible to attribute to interest modeling alone.

    **Illustrative example:** If running and photography each return 50 items, compare the merged 100-item budget to one channel with 100, not 50.

    Sources: [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md)

### Why do Airbnb EBR and MDCNS emphasize negatives without simply taking the highest-scoring unclicked item as the best negative? {#cross-hard-negative-is-not-ground-truth}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Airbnb interprets hard negatives in their journey and behavioral stage. MDCNS uses disagreement across views rather than only Self's preferences. A non-click can reflect underexposure, substitution, or a missing label. A high score means the current model sees similarity, not that the item is certainly irrelevant. Control false negatives, diversity, and sampling budget.

    **Illustrative example:** A user booked one property, but two other suitable properties were sold out. Treating them as definitely irrelevant mistakes inventory outcomes for semantic preferences.

    Sources: [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md) · [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md)

### Why can't a stronger ranker recover an interest missed by retrieval, and where can a new training objective help? {#cross-recall-versus-ranking-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The ranker only sorts existing candidates. YouTube DNN separates the stages; MIMA changes which interests nominate candidates using multi-positive assignments; MDCNS changes the negative gradients received by retrieval representations. Check coverage, fixed-K quality, and downstream ranking separately instead of diagnosing the bottleneck from clicks alone.

    **Illustrative example:** If all 100 candidates are running shoes, a ranker cannot show a camera. Multi-interest retrieval must nominate the camera before ranking can compare its value with the shoes.

    Sources: [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md)
